title: 18. Numeracy & Number Systems: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Apply multiplication before addition when evaluating a whole-number expression.
questions.question: What is \(3+4\times 2\)?
questions.explanation: In the order of operations, multiplication is performed before addition. First multiply: \(4\times 2=8\). Then add: \(3+8=11\). Therefore, \(3+4\times 2=11\).

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses before subtraction.
questions.question: What is \(20-(4\times 3)\)?
questions.explanation: Perform the operation inside the parentheses first: \(4\times 3=12\). Then subtract: \(20-12=8\). Therefore, \(20-(4\times 3)=8\).

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an expression with division and multiplication from left to right.
questions.question: What is \(12\div 4\times 3\)?
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication have the same priority, so evaluate from left to right. First divide: \(12\div 4=3\). Then multiply: \(3\times 3=9\). Therefore, \(12\div 4\times 3=9\).
questions.hint: For division and multiplication together, work from left to right.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Apply multiplication before addition in a whole-number expression.
questions.question: What is \(5+3\times 4\)?
questions.explanation: Multiplication is performed before addition. First multiply: \(3\times 4=12\). Then add: \(5+12=17\). Therefore, \(5+3\times 4=17\).
questions.hint: Do not add first; complete the multiplication before adding.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses, multiplication, and subtraction.
questions.question: What is \((4+5)\times 2-6\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate inside the parentheses: \(4+5=9\). Then multiply: \(9\times 2=18\). Finally subtract: \(18-6=12\). Therefore, \((4+5)\times 2-6=12\).
questions.hint: Complete the parentheses first, then multiply, then subtract.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses and division before addition.
questions.question: What is \(36\div (2+4)+3\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate inside the parentheses: \(2+4=6\). Then divide: \(36\div 6=6\). Finally add: \(6+3=9\). Therefore, \(36\div (2+4)+3=9\).

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses and multiplication before addition.
questions.question: What is \(7+2\times (5-3)\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate inside the parentheses: \(5-3=2\). Then multiply: \(2\times 2=4\). Finally add: \(7+4=11\). Therefore, \(7+2\times (5-3)=11\).
questions.hint: Parentheses first, then multiplication, then addition.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses, division, and multiplication.
questions.question: What is \(24\div (3+3)\times 2\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate inside the parentheses: \(3+3=6\). Then divide: \(24\div 6=4\). Finally multiply: \(4\times 2=8\). Therefore, \(24\div (3+3)\times 2=8\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the parentheses first, then work from left to right for division and multiplication.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a multi-step whole-number expression using the standard order of operations.
questions.question: What is \(6+3\times (7-4)-8\div 4\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate inside the parentheses: \(7-4=3\). Then multiply: \(3\times 3=9\). Then divide: \(8\div 4=2\). Finally evaluate addition and subtraction from left to right: \(6+9-2=13\). Therefore, the value is \(13\).
questions.hint: Parentheses first, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.

questions.concept: Order of Operations with Whole Numbers
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a multi-step expression with two sets of parentheses and mixed operations.
questions.question: What is \((9-4)\times 3+18\div (2+1)\)?
questions.explanation: First evaluate each set of parentheses: \(9-4=5\) and \(2+1=3\). Then multiply: \(5\times 3=15\). Then divide: \(18\div 3=6\). Finally add: \(15+6=21\). Therefore, the value is \(21\).
questions.hint: Evaluate both sets of parentheses first, then perform multiplication and division before addition.
